newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia aviation group, CSFB in $150 mln loan talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia aviation group, CSFB in $150 mln loan talks.

text.p: A Russian financial-industrial group said on Wednesday it is negotiating a $150 million loan with investment bank CS First Boston to finance the production of 20 planes with Russian engines for Russian airlines.
Rosaviakonsortsium chief executive Tatevos Surinov told a news conference the group planned to build 20 Tupolev Tu-204 passenger jets powered by engines from Perm Motors (OAO Permskiye Motory).
The government has given Rosaviakonsortsium financial guarantees for a $150 million loan from foreign creditors, which it is now negotiating with CS First Boston, he said.
"It is the first step to provide Russian airlines with new aircraft," Surinov said.
"We hope Russian carrier Vnukovo Airlines will get the first four or five such aircraft by the end of this year," he said.
He said he was unable to say who the buyers of the other planes would be.
Surinov said CS First Boston might bring other creditors into the loan.
The planes would be produced at AO Aviastar in Ulyanovsk and AO KAPO in Kazan, both members of Rosaviakonsortsium, he said.
Valentin Klimov, head of the Tupolev aircraft design bureau, said each Tu-204 jet would have a basic price of $21.5 million for Russian customers.
He said all 20 jets would be leased from Moscow Aviation International, recently founded by world chess champion Garry Kasparov.
Rosaviakonsortsium was founded in 1995 and currently combines 14 aviation plants, airlines, leasing companies and banks.
